text:
alex: Quick q — if we change a runtime default (e.g. batch_size tweak) that only affects perf, do we bump the patch or leave semver alone and just annotate the release notes? deploy window is tomorrow.

sam: My brain: patch for bugfixes, but perf tweaks are tricky. If it can change latencies/costs for customers, treat as patch so it's explicit.

jamie: For our team: patch = backward-compatible bugfix. Nonfunctional runtime tuning that could change SLOs -> patch. Pure infra deploy (no observable change) -> no version bump.

lucy: Agree with jamie. One extra: use plain semver tags only (`vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`). Avoid `+meta` or `-ops` suffixes; deploy-bot parsing breaks on those.

deploy-bot: notice — new tag pushed: v1.14.3. Canary scheduled for 2026-03-20T14:00Z. To rollback run: `/deploy rollback v1.14.3` :ok_hand:

alex: Good to know. So metadata goes in release notes, not the tag.

sam: Suggest changelog line format for these: `- ops: tuned batch_size to improve throughput (no API change)`

jamie: Edge case: if the default affects model output (e.g. decoding param default), that is a behavior change -> bump minor and gate with evals.

lucy: Yep — anything that can change user-visible outputs should be at least minor. Also add an eval job in CI for those PRs.

alex: Can someone add a short blurb to RELEASES.md so maintainers follow this? I can do the PR but need wording.

eng-release-manager: I'll add this today. Proposed copy: "Patch = bug fixes, non-breaking runtime tweaks, lockfile updates. Minor = new features or changes that can alter outputs or APIs. Tags must be plain semver (vX.Y.Z). Put operational context in the release notes using an `ops:` prefix." Want to tweak?

sam: Looks good. +1

jamie: +1. Also request: deploy-bot could parse `ops:` in release notes and attach it to the rollout page.

deploy-bot: logged issue RB-1423 to add `ops:` label parsing. ETA: 2 sprints.

alex: Perfect. We'll use v1.14.3 for tomorrow; include the `ops:` changelog line. If canary fails we run `/deploy rollback v1.14.3` and notify #incidents.

lucy: :thumbsup:
